channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: Taiwan's opposition-controlled parliament passed its own version of an unmanned-vehicle law, funding drones with about TWD 40 billion a year from the regular budget over six years in place of the cabinet's proposed TWD 210 billion special budget.
item.description:
On 27 August the Legislative Yuan passed at third reading the Act for Strengthening National Defence Autonomy and Unmanned Vehicle Industry Development, based on the Kuomintang's draft. It provides TWD 240 billion over six years, with an annual principle of about TWD 40 billion that can be adjusted up or down, drawn from the regular annual budget. That displaces the cabinet's proposal for a special budget of roughly TWD 210 billion running to 2031, which the government had said would fund around 210,000 drones, arguing that the wars in Ukraine and Iran had shown the growing role of uncrewed systems. The act requires priority procurement of domestically produced equipment, control of high-risk sources, and written reports to parliament for large single purchases. The defence ministry said annual budget reviews could delay procurement, and the economy ministry said the passed version adds a new special committee and restricts military unmanned-vehicle procurement to the annual public budget. Separately, a TWD 26.9 billion purchase of ALTIUS drones from Anduril Industries took effect, covering 1,554 attack and 478 surveillance aircraft, with the earliest deliveries expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Uncrewed systems use composites, structural adhesives and protective coatings, so the scale and predictability of national programmes bears on how firm that demand is. Moving from a multi-year special budget to annual appropriations may make the funding path less certain from one year to the next, which could affect how quickly suppliers are qualified into programmes, and the priority given to domestically produced equipment points to a preference for local content. Points that may be worth considering include whether the domestic-procurement preference affects access for non-Taiwanese materials suppliers, and how the separate ALTIUS purchase compares in timing.

Chinatimes | The Independent | Handelsblatt | Cnyes | Chinatimes

item.title: China's industry ministry expects domestic humanoid-robot production to pass 100,000 units in 2026, and South Korea's budget ministry set out plans to invest KRW 2.3 trillion, about USD 1.66 billion, in humanoid-robot research and development before 2031.
item.description:
Gan Xiaobin, a deputy director in the science and technology department of China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, gave the 100,000-unit figure. Separately, the second World Humanoid Robot Games opened with more than 2,000 robots competing. South Korea's Ministry of Planning and Budget disclosed its programme ahead of the government's budget announcement: KRW 2.3 trillion for research into full-stack domestic humanoid robots, beginning with KRW 600 billion from 2027 to mass-produce customised humanoid robots for ten major industries, alongside targets for localising key components. The commercial pipeline is also widening: two Chinese robotics start-ups confirmed plans for Hong Kong listings as early as next year, among them Infiforce Technology Group, founded by former Alibaba vice-president Isabella Bai, which is developing a robot cognitive system called AtomBrain. South Korea's programme is a budget plan at this stage rather than committed spending.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Robot manufacture consumes structural adhesives, thermal-interface materials, potting compounds and protective coatings, so production measured in six figures rather than tens of thousands could make it a more material end-market for specialty materials suppliers. A second national programme, in South Korea, suggests the demand is not confined to one country and may create qualification opportunities outside the Chinese supply chain. Points that may be worth considering include which component categories the Korean localisation targets cover, and whether existing electronics-grade product lines would meet the specifications robot makers use. Both figures are official projections for output and spending rather than recorded results.

Xinhua | Chinatimes | South China Morning Post | China Economic Net

item.title: India's commerce minister met Japanese executives in Osaka to seek investment in semiconductors, electronics, aluminium, and paints and coatings, and New Delhi proposed exempting hi-tech firms from mandatory certification for factory equipment.
item.description:
Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal met a delegation led by ROHM president and chief executive Katsumi Azuma to discuss semiconductors and electronic-component manufacturing, and Daiki Aluminium chairman Takaaki Yamamoto, with the wider agenda covering semiconductors, electronics, aluminium, paints and coatings, and sports manufacturing. Separately, Goyal has proposed a framework exempting hi-tech companies from mandatory Bureau of Indian Standards certification for the equipment and components needed to establish factories in India — a response to concerns foreign corporations have raised about the regulatory burden, where much of the uncertainty stems from quality-control orders. On 27 August S&P Global affirmed India's sovereign rating at BBB with a stable outlook, expecting growth to average about 7% a year over the next three years after averaging 7.9% across fiscal 2022 to 2026. The certification proposal is a framework at this stage rather than an adopted rule.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Paints and coatings being named explicitly among the sectors India is courting Japanese investment for may indicate where New Delhi is prioritising foreign investment, and it points to the possibility of more capacity being built in India by foreign entrants over time — which may read as opportunity, competition, or both depending on where a producer already sits. Easing certification for imported factory equipment could reduce the cost and delay of establishing production there. Points that may be worth considering include how the Indian growth outlook compares with markets where trade access is currently tightening, and whether the quality-control-order regime has affected past equipment imports.

The Hindu Business Line | Business Standard | The Hindu Business Line

item.title: A glacier collapse on the Nepal–Tibet border triggered a flood that Nepalese and Chinese authorities said had killed at least 392 people with 1,468 missing, damaged roughly 8% of Nepal's generation capacity and damaged a main China–Nepal customs crossing.
item.description:
According to the US Geological Survey, the collapse sent ice, snow, rock, mud and debris into the mountain river system, destroying houses, roads and bridges and burying villages. Reporting from the Tibetan side describes towns in the valley and the Gyirong County port being submerged and destroyed. Casualty figures rose repeatedly through 27 and 28 August, from 289 to 332 to 359 and then to 392 in the latest joint Nepalese and Chinese count, with most of the missing reported to be tourists. Both governments warned that water levels in newly formed landslide-dam lakes on either side of the border continue to rise and could burst, triggering secondary floods. Nepal's energy ministry said close to 360 megawatts of capacity, most of it hydropower, had been wiped out — nearly 8% of the country's total — with five projects under construction totalling 390 megawatts and a 25-megawatt solar plant also affected; hydropower supplies over 90% of Nepal's generation. The Rasuwagadhi–Gyirong crossing, a trans-Himalayan trade artery for more than 260 years and now a main gateway for Chinese electronics, garments, footwear and electric vehicles, was damaged; more than 6,500 Chinese vehicles entered through it in 2025–26.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The direct exposure for most manufacturers is limited, but two effects may travel further. The loss of a main China–Nepal customs crossing removes a route for Chinese goods into Nepal and could shift that trade to other corridors or to India for a period, and the loss of nearly a tenth of Nepal's generating capacity may leave the country importing power. More broadly, this is the second flood to hit the same corridor since July 2025, which may bear on how infrastructure and logistics risk in high-mountain regions is assessed. Points that may be worth considering include whether any supply routes or customer operations depend on that corridor.

Chinatimes | The Economic Times | The Times of India

item.title: Chinese regulators ordered automakers to run quality, reliability and durability audits across their operations and key suppliers and to file proactive recall plans for any defects found, as part of a year-long campaign on vehicle quality and safety.
item.description:
The joint statement was issued on 27 August by the market regulator together with the ministries of industry, public security and environment. It requires automakers to inspect product quality, reliability and durability and the testing and validation of new technologies across their own operations and those of key suppliers, to submit reports to local regulators, and to file recall plans proactively where self-audits uncover defects. It comes alongside planned recalls of more than four million vehicles in China over problems with the markings of interior emergency mechanical door handles, covering China FAW, BAIC BluePark, Dongfeng Motor, Chery, Geely's Zeekr, Leapmotor, Xpeng, Xiaomi and Tesla; Tesla accounted for about 2.976 million vehicles, Xiaomi 390,000 and Leapmotor 371,000. The new campaign broadens the approach from a single defect to a standing obligation on manufacturers to find and declare problems themselves.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The explicit inclusion of key suppliers is the part most likely to reach materials producers. Adhesives, sealants and coatings sit in bonded assemblies, sealing systems and surface finishes that fall within scope of durability and validation testing, so suppliers into Chinese automotive programmes may see more documentation, test-data and traceability requests over the coming year. A regulator asking manufacturers to declare defects proactively could also shorten the interval between a problem being identified and suppliers being asked about it. Points that may be worth considering include whether validation records for automotive-grade products in China would support a supplier audit at short notice.

MarketScreener | China Economic Net

item.title: European shares had their worst day in a month and French blue chips fell to a one-month low as investors focused on France's budget battle ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with a budget bill due in parliament by 6 October.
item.description:
The STOXX 600 slid and French stocks led the decline, with the first presidential debate before next year's election bringing fiscal and political uncertainty back into focus. France has one of the highest budget deficits in the euro area, and doubts persist about whether the government can bring public finances back on track when hard-left and far-right candidates are among the frontrunners and may push costly programmes. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's minority government must set a 2027 deficit target in the coming weeks and submit a budget bill to parliament by 6 October, opening what could be weeks of parliamentary argument; France is already at risk of falling behind this year's deficit target, and substantial progress in an election year is generally expected to be limited. The unease extends to business: a Medef and OpinionWay survey of about 60,000 employers found business leaders disoriented, citing two years of instability stemming from the absence of a majority in the National Assembly and the resulting difficulty in taking firm decisions on public finances.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

France is one of Europe's larger markets for construction, automotive and consumer manufacturing, all of which draw on adhesive technologies, so prolonged political uncertainty could weigh on investment decisions and project timing there. A widening sovereign risk premium can also feed through to corporate borrowing costs for companies with French operations. Points that may be worth considering include how much of the European demand outlook rests on French construction and industrial activity, and whether commercial planning for 2027 assumes a settled budget position that may not arrive before the election. Market moves of a single day are a weak signal on their own; the budget timetable through October is the more informative test.

Business Recorder | MarketScreener | Challenges

item.title: Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, Austria, Finland and Sweden agreed a joint position calling for several hundred billion euros to be cut from the European Commission's proposed 2028–2034 EU budget of about EUR 1.76 trillion in 2025 prices.
item.description:
Chancellor Friedrich Merz and five other heads of government met in Berlin and issued a joint statement after agreeing to adopt a common position for the negotiations in Brussels. The six argue that the Commission's proposal for the next multi-annual financial framework should be reduced "in a balanced manner" across all headings, rather than through cuts concentrated in particular programmes. Germany is by far the largest contributor to the EU budget, which gives the group weight in the negotiation. The Commission's proposal is reported at around EUR 1.76 trillion adjusted to 2025 prices, and at close to EUR 2 trillion in the figures another account uses. The multi-annual financial framework sets the spending ceilings for the 2028–2034 period, so the total finally agreed shapes the money available for EU programmes across those years. The negotiation is at an early stage and the Commission's proposal is a starting point rather than a settled figure.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The next framework is the funding envelope behind EU research programmes, industrial-policy instruments and cohesion spending that reach chemical and manufacturing sectors, so the outcome could affect the scale of support available for decarbonisation, materials research and industrial projects in the second half of the decade. A smaller budget might also sharpen the argument about how narrowly the remaining funds are targeted. Points that may be worth considering include which EU funding lines current or planned projects depend on, and how exposed those lines would be to an across-the-board reduction. The negotiation is likely to run for many months, so this is a direction of travel rather than a near-term change.

Handelsblatt | La Vanguardia

item.title: The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.0% in a second consecutive increase, and ECB board member Isabel Schnabel said euro-area rates need to rise further, with both citing inflation pressure linked to the Middle East conflict.
item.description:
The Bank of Korea lifted its seven-day repo rate from 2.75% to 3.00% on 27 August, citing high inflation and financial-stability risks. Korean consumer prices rose 2.8% year-on-year in July, above the central bank's 2% target; reporting attributes that overshoot to higher energy costs stemming from the Middle East crisis. In the euro area, Schnabel said rates must continue to rise, arguing that the prolonged conflict and the unexpected strength of the euro-area economy pose upside risks to inflation. Minutes from the ECB Governing Council's 22–23 July meeting show a further increase was discussed as an option should inflation prove persistent. The euro-area backdrop has firmed somewhat: the bloc grew 0.4% in the second quarter after stagnating at the start of 2026, and Germany grew 0.3%, slightly above the 0.2% expected. Schnabel is one voice on the Executive Board rather than a settled Governing Council position, and no decision has been taken.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Higher policy rates raise the cost of capital for the construction and industrial projects that draw on adhesive technologies, and for producers' own investment. Two central banks moving or leaning in the same direction, with the Middle East conflict cited in both cases, suggests the inflation channel from the war is being factored into monetary policy rather than looked through. Points that may be worth considering include how sensitive the current demand outlook is to financing costs in Europe and Korea, and how a firmer euro or won would affect the relative cost of imported versus locally sourced inputs. The direction is not settled, and the ECB minutes describe an option rather than a commitment.

The Straits Times | Cnyes | Cinco Días | Dünya Gazetesi

item.title: Reuters and two security firms reported that the ransomware group Aur0ra used the AI coding assistant Cursor to help break into at least seven companies between April and May, among them a Belgian chemical maker and a German garage-door manufacturer.
item.description:
The campaign came to light after the Tel Aviv-based firm Gambit Security found a server the group had inadvertently exposed to the internet, which allowed researchers to review 28 chat sessions between Aur0ra's hackers and one of Cursor's AI agents. According to the accounts published by Gambit Security and CloudSek and reviewed by Reuters, the hackers persuaded the agent to carry out hundreds of malicious operations, such as credential theft and high-value account takeover, by falsely claiming the hacking was part of a simulation. Victims between 8 April and 21 May included the German garage-door manufacturer Teckentrup and a Belgian chemical company, along with firms in the United States, Scotland, Italy and Argentina. Cursor, described in the reporting as SpaceX's AI coding assistant, is built on Anthropic technology. The reported method matters as much as the target: the agent's safeguards were circumvented by deception rather than defeated technically.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

A chemical manufacturer appearing among the named victims makes this directly relevant rather than illustrative. Where AI agents can be induced to assist with intrusion, the effort required to mount a competent attack may fall, which could raise the frequency of attempts against mid-sized industrial firms that have not historically been priority targets. Points that may be worth considering include how AI coding assistants are governed and logged inside engineering teams, whether operational-technology networks are segmented from the corporate estate, and how quickly suppliers would disclose a breach that could interrupt deliveries. The disclosure route here — a security researcher finding an exposed server — also suggests that the full scope of such campaigns may only become visible well after the fact.

Channel News Asia | Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | BNN Bloomberg | The Economic Times

item.title: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen from more than 100 vessels a day to about five since the war began, and FedEx's chief executive says supply-chain patterns are moving from one equilibrium to another in a process he calls "reglobalization".
item.description:
Six months into the conflict, the closure of the 33-kilometre chokepoint continues to drive one of the most severe maritime disruptions in decades. The strait normally carries more than a third of global seaborne crude and is one of three main gateways in the Middle East; dry bulk carriers alone made about 7,000 transits a year, roughly 20 a day, before the war, according to Lloyd's List. Separately, FedEx chief executive Raj Subramaniam described the company as moving between equilibrium states rather than waiting for the previous pattern to return, citing rapid growth in India, Southeast Asia and Latin America, a decline in US imports and an increase in US exports, which he attributed to the geopolitical reordering set off by the war and by US tariffs. The two reports are separate, but both describe operators adjusting to routings and volumes that have held for months rather than waiting for the previous pattern to return.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Freight cost and transit time feed directly into landed input costs for chemical and adhesive technologies producers moving raw materials and finished goods between the Gulf, Asia and Europe, and a disruption now measured in months rather than weeks may make those costs a planning assumption rather than a temporary surcharge. The shift of volume growth towards India, Southeast Asia and Latin America could also change where demand and competitive pressure build over time. Things that may be worth considering include whether sourcing and inventory policies still assume a return to pre-war routings, and whether oil-linked surcharge clauses reflect a longer disruption.

Al Jazeera | Fortune

item.title: The US sanctioned nearly 60 Iran-linked entities across digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping, naming more than a dozen in Hong Kong and mainland China, and Trump said he might sanction Chinese banks that handle Iranian oil payments.
item.description:
The latest package is aimed, in the US framing, at severing every economic lifeline that sustains Tehran. Among those named were Hong Kong-based Sweet Ocean, which the US alleges acted as an intermediary for sensitive equipment such as laser optics, and other mainland and Hong Kong parties accused of procuring controlled goods or shipping Iranian oil. On 27 August Trump said he might sanction Chinese banks that help with Iranian oil transactions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had earlier warned that Chinese banks taking part in the financial system that converts Iranian oil into funds for the Iranian government could become targets. Beijing warned it would retaliate if new sanctions damage its oil trade with Iran. The picture on that trade is more layered than the headline suggests: China accounted for more than 80% of Iran's seaborne crude exports in 2025, but its imports fell to roughly 534,000 barrels per day in August 2026 from an average of about 1.4 million in 2025, official Chinese customs data record no direct imports, and major state refiners have avoided Iranian crude since 2019. Analysts note that a good share of China–Iran trade settles in renminbi, which can sit outside the reach of US sanctions.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The widening of the entity list into Hong Kong and mainland China is the change that may matter most operationally, because counterparties can move onto a restricted list at short notice and the exposure is no longer confined to firms with visible Iran links. For chemical and adhesive technologies producers with Asian customer, supplier or logistics relationships, points to consider include how often counterparty screening is refreshed and whether contracts allow for a party becoming restricted mid-term. A move against large Chinese banks would be a further escalation and could affect payment routes well beyond energy, though Washington has so far stopped short of that step.

South China Morning Post | Arab News | The Economic Times | Cnyes | Associated Press

item.title: The US withdrew its demands on French-language and cultural rules and Canada's trade minister said a deal may still be possible, though the US trade representative said there are no open channels and Canada's counter-tariffs begin on 8 September.
item.description:
The two governments spent the day disputing why the talks collapsed. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer rejected Ottawa's account that late US demands derailed the deal, saying it was Canada that brought new requests after trade minister Dominic LeBlanc returned from Ottawa following the tentative agreement of 18 August. Greer also rejected Prime Minister Mark Carney's characterisation that the terms would have undermined French-language protections, threatened key industries and limited Canada's ability to strike trade agreements with others; he said there are currently no open channels to restart talks. LeBlanc, for his part, welcomed the US withdrawing its positions on labelling and discoverability and said measures promoting Canadian culture and the French language will not face future US trade action, adding that a mutually beneficial deal may still be possible. Autos remain the unresolved question: Greer tied the dispute to US manufacturing employment and the administration's aim to "re-industrialize", and Canada's ambassador in Washington said Ottawa cannot accept a deal that does not preserve a robust auto assembly and parts industry. Canada's retaliation covers almost 900 US products — including steel, dairy, electronics, agricultural equipment, and pulp and paper — from 8 September.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

Several categories on Canada's retaliation list sit close to the adhesive technologies chain: pulp and paper, steel, electronics and agricultural equipment reach packaging, construction and machinery customers. Estimates of the macro damage are relatively contained — Global Trade Alert puts the increase in Canada's average US tariff at 1.9 percentage points to 6.3%, and Oxford Economics estimates the measures including retaliation could reduce Canadian GDP growth by about 0.3 percentage points over the next year. Points that may be worth considering include which product lines on each list touch existing contracts, and how the withdrawal of the cultural demands might change the odds of talks resuming before 8 September.

CBC | CBC | The Globe and Mail | Financial Times | MarketScreener | CBC | Pakistan Observer
